actions.action: Check soil moisture with the finger test before watering
Water thoroughly and deeply when the soil feels dry
Use a pot with drainage holes and keep the saucer free of excess water
Slide the plant out of its pot to inspect the roots
If roots are compacted, prune unhealthy roots, loosen them and repot in a larger container with premium potting mix
If roots are rotten and diseased, replace the plant
Amend the soil to correct pH per the test recommendations
Examine the yellowing pattern to identify a nutrient deficiency
Feed with a balanced controlled-release plant food (10-10-10)
If magnesium or sulfur is lacking, apply Epsom salt
If iron is lacking, apply an iron-containing fertilizer

verdict.reason: The answer is a generic yellow-leaf article that treats the yellowing as a problem (watering, roots, pH, nutrients) rather than recognizing a normal aging leaf on a healthy plant, it never mentions trellising, and its suggestions are mostly conditional or safeguarded, so they are unnecessary rather than likely harmful.
